solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Penguins are rarely so exhausting, as before

parts.note: exhausting work is hard work
to go back to something is to return to how it was before

explanation.surface: A remark that Penguin books are seldom tiring, just as was said earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: Penguin is a publisher famous for paperbacks, so its books are seldom bound in stiff covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin Books built its name on cheap paperbacks, so rigid-covered editions are the exception there.

clue.text: Archetypal Scot loses the head with strict Pennsylvanian?

indicators.note: loses the head means the first letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Hamish is the stereotypical Scottish name in jokes

explanation.surface: A typical Scotsman is beheaded alongside a stern resident of Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a strict Anabaptist community, many living in Pennsylvania; the query marks the example.

clue.text: Board's place to chew things over in civilised fashion, perhaps

definitions.text: Board's place to chew things over in civilised fashion, perhaps

parts.words: Board's place to chew things over in civilised fashion, perhaps
parts.note: a board is a table, and chewing over can mean eating as well as discussing, as at a formal meal

explanation.surface: Where a company's directors calmly discuss business.
explanation.walkthrough: Board suggests directors and chew over suggests discussion; read literally, it is a table where people eat a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The table at which a family or guests sit for the main evening meal, where talk accompanies eating.

clue.text: Last in spite of expectations

definitions.meaning: coming at the very end, behind everything else
nevertheless, contrary to what was anticipated

explanation.surface: Finishing at the back despite what everyone predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it means behind everything else; as an idiom it means nevertheless or despite expectations.

clue.text: Stay cool and don't lose everything!

definitions.meaning: remain calm and not lose one's temper
literally avoid being stripped of every possession, down to the last garment

explanation.surface: Advice to a gambler: keep calm and avoid going bust.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay calm; read literally it is to avoid losing even the clothes on your back.

clue.text: Give in pliant manner

definitions.meaning: an adverb from supple: bendily, flexibly

explanation.surface: Yield in a flexible way.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means provide; the rarer adverb formed from supple means flexibly.

clue.text: Southern water where friendly bombs were wanted

parts.note: a lough is an Irish lake or sea inlet

explanation.surface: A southern lake was once the target of welcome air raids.
explanation.walkthrough: John Betjeman's 1937 poem about this English town opens 'Come, friendly bombs, and fall on Slough!'
explanation.definitionFit: Betjeman's poem invited friendly bombs to fall on this Berkshire town, the target he wished them on.

clue.text: Athenian's letter is upside-down in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the run of letters in upside-down is taken

explanation.surface: A Greek letter is inverted in places.
explanation.walkthrough: Upside-down looks like a reversal signal, but the letters sit forwards inside that very word.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is the twenty-third letter of the Greek alphabet, used by Athenians.

clue.text: John feels a brew of tea

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: brew of means the letters of feels a are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named John senses a cup of tea being made.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a man's name; it is slang for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea sold as loose dried leaves rather than in bags is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: A small seal is back with good catch

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word is from right to left

parts.note: a net is used to catch fish, and a catch can be a net haul

explanation.surface: A little seal makes a comeback by snaring a fine meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a seal the animal; the definition is a seal for stamping wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a small seal, typically set in a ring and pressed into wax.

clue.text: Come on it changes, eg :0)

indicators.note: changes says the letters of come on it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An encouraging cry as something shifts, with a smiley tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The typed face :0) is an example of a small picture made of keyboard characters that conveys a mood.

clue.text: Find tailored hose in this

indicators.note: tailored suggests something altered or reworked, so the letters of hose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hint that the stockings will be discovered inside this item of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: rearranged hose gives the answer, and hose (socks) are found in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Socks or stockings are worn inside a piece of footwear, so hose are found in it.

clue.text: Presumably few go over this high-blown plot?

definitions.text: Presumably few go over this high-blown plot?

parts.words: Presumably few go over this high-blown plot?
parts.note: a plot of planted ground set high up on a building, which few people would walk over since it sits atop the house

explanation.surface: Doubt that many people would read past such an overblown storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot and go over suggest a story being read; the plot is a garden patch, and high-blown means perched up on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden laid out on top of a building is literally a high plot that few people cross.

clue.text: Etonian rigs renewed surrender

indicators.note: renewed means the letters of etonian rigs are made over afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A pupil from Eton fixes a renewed capitulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up a post or yielding to fate are both forms of giving in, a synonym of surrender.

clue.text: I shall tuck into gum drop

indicators.note: tuck into means the short form of I shall is placed inside the glue word

parts.note: gum is an adhesive, as is paste
I shall contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will eat some chewing gum and then let it fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck into reads as eating, but it is the container signal; drop is the noun, a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small lozenge or sweet, also called a drop, as in a cough drop.

clue.text: Contract mere agent set into motion

indicators.note: set into motion means the letters of mere agent are stirred about

explanation.surface: An ordinary agent puts a deal into action.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding agreement between parties.

clue.text: Get rid of outhouse

definitions.meaning: to cast off or discard, as a snake its skin
a small hut or outbuilding in a garden

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear away the garden outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means cast off, as skin or leaves; the noun is a simple garden hut.

clue.text: Available around noon, jerk becomes mad

indicators.note: around means the available word goes round the noon letter

parts.note: something free is available
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A free man about midday becomes crazed by a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means wildly frantic, close to frenzied or mad.

clue.text: Grouch runs into growler of old

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a growler was a Victorian four-wheeled horse-drawn cab
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A grumpy person dashes into an old grumbler.
explanation.walkthrough: Growler sounds like another grumbler, but historically it was London slang for a four-wheeled hackney cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is a cantankerous person, and as a verb to grouch or complain.

clue.text: Get rid of unruly roughs following female

indicators.note: unruly says the letters of roughs are put in disorder

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in p. 12 f.

explanation.surface: Dismissing a gang of disorderly thugs who are chasing a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as SHRUGO (roughs rearranged) plus F for following and F for female.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug off something is to dismiss or throw it off, a phrasal synonym of discarding.

clue.text: Old planes reached the borders of Leeds

parts.note: came means arrived at or reached

indicators.note: the borders of means taking the outside letters of leeds

explanation.surface: Vintage aircraft arrived at the outskirts of a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sopwith Camel was a British First World War fighter biplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Sopwith Camels were First World War biplanes, so they are old aircraft.

clue.text: Passing over translation of Gideon et al

indicators.note: translation of here means turning the letters of Gideon et al into a new form

explanation.surface: A Bible passage about Gideon and his companions being rendered in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: Passing over suggests ignoring; here it means handing on authority or duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrusting tasks or authority to others is handing them over, the act of devolving power.

clue.text: He leaves sincere Bohemian

indicators.note: leaves means the letters of he depart from the synonym

parts.note: hearty thanks are sincere thanks

explanation.surface: A man walks out on someone heartfelt and unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: Bohemian is not the Czech region but a style: artistic and unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affecting an artistic, unconventional lifestyle is described with this informal adjective.

clue.text: Wield minute charming symbol, say

parts.note: to tote a gun is to carry or wield it

explanation.surface: Brandish a lucky charm for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem with protective or sacred power, an example of a charm-like symbol.

clue.text: Building pieces in principle

indicators.note: in means the chess-piece word goes inside the belief word

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or doctrine
chessmen are pieces, so men are pieces

explanation.surface: Constructing something bit by bit, at least in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: In principle looks like a phrase meaning theoretically, but principle is the outer word and in the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: She's up and down carrying milk?

definitions.text: She's up and down carrying milk?

parts.words: She's up and down carrying milk?
parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman who is moody while carrying a milk bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: she is a female sheep, up and down says the three letters read the same either way in this down entry, and she gives milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a she that produces milk, and its three letters read the same either way.

clue.text: Sucked in by fools, son gets another card turned over

indicators.note: sucked in by means the son letter is drawn inside the word for fools

parts.note: twits are silly people, fools
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy conned by idiots draws a further card in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In pontoon (the British name for blackjack) to twist is to ask for another card dealt face up.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as pontoon, twisting is asking the dealer for an extra card.

clue.text: Area is outside next European capital

indicators.note: outside means the two outer pieces wrap around the word for next

parts.note: is shortens to 's, giving S
then means next, as in first this, then that

explanation.surface: A region lies beyond the next city in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Is is used in its contracted form 's, leaving just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Appropriate noun preceding a setter, Jason say

indicators.note: preceding places the first word ahead of the rest

parts.note: to appropriate is to steal, informally to nick
N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A suitable word comes before the compiler, Jason for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Appropriate looks like an adjective (suitable); it is the verb meaning steal. Jason is this setter's pen-name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason is the pseudonym this compiler uses, an assumed name of the kind people adopt informally.
